assertions.name: confinement_lp_is_homogeneous
assertions.source: x*(n) = (n/n0) x*(n0) and ||offset||/n constant across the tested net values — the cone-slice structure of G x >= 0

description: Tests whether the confinement operator-selection LP's solution offset can carry theta_K. The Frobenius constraint Gx >= 0 is a homogeneous cone, so the feasible set at net n_target is n_target times a fixed polytope; with t and G knot-independent (pyhecke.gram) and only n_target = |tr_M(K)| varying, the optimum and hence the offset scale exactly. Verified numerically. Consequence: two knots give PARALLEL offsets — the angle is knot-independent and the magnitude is proportional to tr_M(K), so the pair supplies one number, not two, and is ratio-shaped. AfreeThetaConstraint.ratio_attained proves such a candidate unfalsifiable. Escape: a formulation with knot-dependent t or G is not homogeneous and is not excluded. Nothing fitted.

data.program: min t.x s.t. 1^T x = n_target, G x >= 0 (prop:operator-selection-lp)
data.why_it_matters: homogeneity makes the offset direction knot-independent and the magnitude proportional to tr_M(K); the pair is therefore ratio-shaped and unfalsifiable by ratio_attained
data.the_only_escape: put the braid's operator content into the OBJECTIVE t or the GRAM G, not merely the net constraint n_target; that breaks homogeneity and is not excluded here
data.verdict: THE CONFINEMENT LP IS HOMOGENEOUS, SO ITS OFFSET CANNOT CARRY ϑ_K — a structural exclusion of the canonical formulation, established before any fitting. The Frobenius constraint G x >= 0 is a CONE, so the feasible set at net n_target is exactly n_target times the fixed polytope at 1. Measured: x*(n) = (n/n0) x*(n0) to 4.5e-12 and the offset direction is constant to 0 rad, with ||offset||/n constant. Since t and G are knot-INDEPENDENT (properties of the H_3 basis at q0) and only n_target = |tr_M(K)| varies, two knots produce PARALLEL offsets: the ANGLE carries zero knot information — it is literally the same number for every knot — and the MAGNITUDE is a fixed constant times tr_M(K). So the pair (magnitude, angle) supplies ONE knot-dependent number, not two, and its knot-to-knot content is the ratio tr_M(K1)/tr_M(K2). AfreeThetaConstraint.ratio_attained proves a ratio-shaped candidate is unfalsifiable — it names an A_omega rather than testing one. This route, in this formulation, therefore cannot clear the falsifiability bar. THE ESCAPE, and it is the only one: a formulation whose t or G is itself knot-dependent is NOT homogeneous and is NOT excluded. That means the braid's own operator content must enter the OBJECTIVE or the GRAM, not merely the net constraint. SCOPE (a): this excludes the canonical scalar-net formulation as the corpus builds it, not the proposal. Nothing fitted; nothing wired.
